correctness.rationale: Proved without computational extrapolation: all-positive arc labels forbid mixed in/out vertices, forcing source–sink bipartite selected graph; a selected three-edge path has the two outer positive labels forcing the middle arc positive, contradicting shattering. A bipartite connected graph with no three-edge path is a star. Conversely assign the center/leaf vertex bits independently to realize every prescribed pattern. For one-descent ranking, any permutation is two increasing runs, encoding the arc predicate exactly. The count \(2^n-n\) follows by quotienting n+1 initial-segment encodings of the identity. A spanning star gives lower bound \(n-1\); cardinality <2^n gives matching Littlestone upper bound; exponential-formula recurrence enumerates every eligible forest. Exhaustive verification independently checked all supports through n=6 and all 729 oriented graphs on four vertices.

originality.rationale: Direct structural implication comparisons with four relevant primary sources and six actual semantic research queries found no theorem that characterizes exactly the oriented-star-forest traces of arbitrary directed cuts, nor the one-descent comparison support polynomial. The comparison was made by concept universe and logical implication: prior graph-orientation shattering concerns edge orientation variables; prior maximum-dicut work concerns maximum cardinality of cuts, not traces; prior permutation VC uses a different k-point full-order-realization definition; prior preference elicitation concerns distribution-aware average number of sorting queries. Residual possible coverage under two-literal Boolean formula trace language is explicitly acknowledged.
residual_risks: No exhaustive worldwide historical-priority assessment; an older result on directed-cut traces, rank-one Boolean products, or signed two-literal conjunctions might imply the star-forest theorem.
Raz full text was not read, but the official abstract confirms its definition differs; any indirect implication beyond this statement has not been excluded.
A potentially earlier open preprint of the 2021 focal paper may exist; the official May 18, 2021 publication date is the earliest independently verified publication date used here.

value.rationale: Complete forbidden-configuration and constructive realization theorem for all oriented graphs, rather than a single VC scalar or routine k=small computation. For a natural sparse ranking family it produces an all-degree labeled exponential generating function and rigid two-star maximum support theorem for every order. It identifies a structural contrast—full symmetric-group comparison learning dimensions remain \(n-1\) in a much smaller \(2^n-n\) family—useful when choosing restricted query models. It explicitly separates support combinatorics from adaptive dimension and from distribution-aware elicitation.
